newsitem.title: USA: Chevron extends healthcare to gay partners.
newsitem.headline: Chevron extends healthcare to gay partners.

text.p: San Francisco-based Chevron Corp joined other corporate giants by announcing this week it would extend domestic partners' benefits to most of its U.S. employees, regardless of sexual preference.
Chevron is the first major U.S. oil firm to offer such a program, which will take effect January 1998, a company spokeswoman said.

The 117-year-old company follows in the footsteps of BankAmerica and other Bay-area firms who have offered similar programs since San Franicsco passed an ordinance in late 1996 requiring companies doing business with the city to offer equal partner benefits, regardless of sexual preference.

"This helps us attract and retain the best people to better serve our diverse customer base, which is essential for our continued business success," said Ron Kiskis, vice president of human resources.
Chevron's benefits will include medical, dental, dependent life insurance, relocation, and leave-time for bereavement or care of sick partners.
Chevron Corp has about 26,250 employees in the U.S. and 35,310 worldwide.

About 8,000 to 10,000 private-sector businesses have contracts and do work for San Francisco, according to Jeff Sheehy, who helped author the ordiance and serves as president of the Harvey Milk Lesbian/Gay/Bisexual Democratic Club.
"It's fantastic," Sheehy said when told about Chevron's announcement.
"Chevron is leading the way in what is traditionally a conservative industry," he said
Should companies fail to offer or promise equal health benefits to same-sex partners by June 1997, they would be barred from bidding for city contracts.
Sheehy said Pacific Gas & Electric, a huge San Francisco-based utility, is expected to offer a domestic partners package "anyday".
